pairs.title: ABAP RAP or SAP CAP for an AI-enabled application
pairs.question: Where should the business logic and data model of a new AI-enabled SAP application live?

options.name: ABAP RAP (ABAP RESTful Application Programming Model)

capability_fit.text: Business objects with behaviour, authorization and OData exposure inside ABAP; a natural home when the data and logic already live in ABAP / S/4HANA.

sap_alignment.text: Documented SAP-standard model for ABAP-based apps, including generated UI services.

hands_on.text: Needs an ABAP system. ADT tooling was exercised in project test runs on a private ABAP Trial; this public edition cannot run ABAP.

access.text: An ABAP environment (for example a trial) and ADT. Not available to anonymous visitors.

licensing.text: Depends on the ABAP environment you use. Check SAP's current terms; not verified here.

dependencies.text: ABAP runtime, ADT, authorizations; AI calls need an outbound service or SAP AI API.

limitations.text: Not a model runtime: AI capabilities are consumed through services you call.

confidence.text: LOW to MEDIUM: documentation and public tutorials only; nothing executed here.

next_step.text: Run the public knowledge lookup for RAP, then the tutorial on a trial ABAP system.

capability_fit.text: CDS-modelled services with OData and (via a plugin) MCP exposure; suited to new cloud-side services and agent-facing APIs.

sap_alignment.text: SAP's application programming model for cloud-native services; see the CAP documentation.

hands_on.text: Runs locally with Node.js. The project ran a local CAP service with OData and MCP on fabricated data in its own test runs; the public edition shows the technique only on a synthetic lab.

access.text: Node.js and project-local packages; no SAP system is needed to prototype.

licensing.text: The @sap/cds packages carry an SAP developer licence (test / non-productive use). Productive use needs an SAP-licensed platform; check current terms.

dependencies.text: Node.js, CDS compiler/runtime, a database plug-in; BTP services for production.

limitations.text: Does not run inside the ABAP stack; reaching ABAP data needs integration.

confidence.text: MEDIUM for the local prototype (observed in project test runs on synthetic data); LOW for tenant behaviour.

next_step.text: Run the synthetic billing lab, then repeat the pattern against your own CAP project.

priorities.text: My data and business logic already live in ABAP / S/4HANA
priorities.because: RAP keeps logic next to ABAP data and authorizations.

priorities.text: I need a hands-on path on my own machine today
priorities.because: CAP prototypes run locally with Node.js and no SAP system.

priorities.text: I want to expose records to agents through an MCP surface
priorities.because: An MCP plugin for CAP is published; RAP has no equivalent verified here.

priorities.text: My team is ABAP-first and the target is an ABAP environment
priorities.because: It reuses ABAP skills and tooling.

pairs.title: ADT MCP or CAP MCP for agent-assisted development
pairs.question: Which MCP surface should an engineering agent use, and for what?

capability_fit.text: Agent-assisted ABAP/RAP development: generators, creation, ATC and transport workflows.

sap_alignment.text: Exposes ABAP development tooling to MCP clients.

hands_on.text: Project test run on a private ABAP Trial: 20 tools; an authenticated read-only listing of generators and creatable object types worked. No repository-browsing tool was present, the server advertised no read-only hints, and no SAP object readback was obtained.

access.text: Local server, an authenticated session to an ABAP system and a token held by that system's owner. Not available here.

licensing.text: Depends on the ABAP system and tooling licence; not verified here.

dependencies.text: Eclipse ADT or equivalent host, ABAP system connection, token.

limitations.text: Most tools create, activate, fix or transport; a client must allowlist read-only tools itself.

confidence.text: LOW: single private observation, not independently verified, not reproducible publicly.

next_step.text: On your own trial: list tools, review each, allowlist read-only ones, compare with Eclipse ADT.

capability_fit.text: Exposes a CAP service's model and data to agents through a small, bounded tool set.

hands_on.text: Project test run: a local service exposed exactly describe and query; mutating requests were refused for read-only entities.

access.text: Node.js and the CAP project; no SAP system.

licensing.text: Apache-2.0 plugin; it runs on @sap/cds, which has its own SAP developer licence.

limitations.text: Only as safe as the service model: entities must be declared read-only.

confidence.text: MEDIUM for the local prototype on synthetic data; LOW beyond that.

next_step.text: Run the synthetic lab, then model your own entities as read-only and inspect the MCP tools list.

priorities.text: The agent must help create or change ABAP/RAP objects
priorities.because: ADT MCP exposes creation, generator and transport workflows.

priorities.text: The agent only needs to read data from a service I own
priorities.because: CAP MCP exposes a small describe/query surface that can be kept read-only.

priorities.text: I have no SAP system to connect to yet
priorities.because: It runs without any SAP system.

priorities.text: I need a read-only boundary I can verify
priorities.because: The tool set is tiny; ADT MCP needs a client-side allowlist because it advertises no hints.

pairs.title: Custom AI extension or a managed SAP AI service
pairs.question: Should the AI capability be built on your own model service or on an SAP-managed AI service?

options.name: Custom AI extension (your own model service)

capability_fit.text: Full control over model choice, prompts and data flow; useful for narrow, well-bounded tasks.

sap_alignment.text: Fits SAP extension principles when it stays loosely coupled to the core.

hands_on.text: The public synthetic lab shows deterministic rules and where a model could add value; it runs no model.

access.text: Access to a model endpoint you choose; credentials are yours to protect.

licensing.text: Model and hosting terms are yours; check data-use and AI-training clauses of any SAP developer tooling you build on.

dependencies.text: Model hosting, evaluation harness, security review.

limitations.text: You own evaluation, safety, monitoring and compliance.

confidence.text: LOW: general reasoning, no SAP-specific evidence executed.

next_step.text: Define a deterministic baseline first (the synthetic lab), then test whether a model beats it.

options.name: Managed SAP AI service (SAP AI Core / Generative AI Hub)

capability_fit.text: SAP-managed access to models with SAP governance and integration points.

sap_alignment.text: Documented SAP AI platform on BTP.

hands_on.text: Needs a BTP entitlement. NOT verified in the public edition; no call is made.

access.text: SAP BTP account with the relevant entitlement and service key.

licensing.text: Chargeable service; current plans and prices are on SAP's pages and are not reproduced here.

dependencies.text: BTP subaccount, entitlements, SDK or REST access.

limitations.text: Availability of trial or free usage must be checked on SAP's current pages; NOT_VERIFIED here.

confidence.text: LOW: documentation only; no execution evidence in this edition.

next_step.text: Check entitlement on your BTP account, then run a minimal read-only inventory call.

priorities.text: I need SAP-managed governance and integration
priorities.because: SAP's managed AI platform is documented to provide it.

priorities.text: I need full control over the model and data flow
priorities.because: A custom service lets you choose and host the model.

priorities.text: I have no BTP entitlement today
priorities.because: The managed service requires an entitlement.

priorities.text: I first want a deterministic baseline to beat
priorities.because: A simple custom rule baseline needs no platform.

pairs.title: SAPUI5 / Fiori or a generic front end
pairs.question: Which front-end approach fits an SAP-connected application?

capability_fit.text: SAP design system, controls, data binding to OData, and Fiori elements for annotation-driven UIs.

sap_alignment.text: SAP's standard UI technology and tooling, including a published UI5 MCP server.

hands_on.text: Project test run: a small UI5 app on a local CAP service rendered and read OData in a real browser; the official UI5 manifest validator found real defects that were fixed.

access.text: Node.js tooling; the UI5 runtime is served from SAP's public CDN.

licensing.text: OpenUI5 is open source; SAPUI5 and some typings carry SAP developer licence terms.

dependencies.text: UI5 runtime and tooling; an OData or REST back end.

limitations.text: Learning curve; theming and controls follow SAP conventions.

confidence.text: MEDIUM for the local prototype (observed in project test runs); LOW for launchpad integration.

next_step.text: Validate your manifest with the UI5 tooling, then bind to your service.

options.name: Generic front end (for example React or Vue)

capability_fit.text: Flexible UX and a large ecosystem; no SAP-specific controls out of the box.

sap_alignment.text: Not an SAP-standard UI; Fiori launchpad integration and design compliance are yours to build.

licensing.text: Per library; no SAP licence involved for the UI layer itself.

dependencies.text: A build chain and an API the UI can call; accessibility and i18n are yours.

limitations.text: Accessibility, theming, localization and SAP UX conformance need your own effort.

next_step.text: Prototype one screen against the same OData service and compare effort.

priorities.text: It must run inside SAP Fiori launchpad with SAP design conformance
priorities.because: It is SAP's standard UI technology.

priorities.text: I want declarative binding to an OData service
priorities.because: UI5 has an OData V4 model and Fiori elements.

priorities.text: My team already ships React/Vue products
priorities.because: It reuses existing skills and pipelines.

priorities.text: I need a highly custom user experience outside SAP conventions
priorities.because: It is not bound to SAP control conventions.
